## Berlin Deposit Dispute Checklist

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg

You can handle this best by staying factual, documenting everything, and asking your landlord to justify each deduction in writing.

## What to Gather Before You Reply

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg

- Move-in and move-out handover protocols, especially any notes about pre-existing wall marks or cleaning condition
- Dated photos or videos from move-out showing walls, floors, bathroom, kitchen, and overall cleanliness
- Any messages with the landlord or agent about the condition of the flat before and after move-out
- Your lease, deposit agreement, and any cleaning or repair clauses
- Receipts for professional cleaning, repairs, or supplies if you already paid for anything
- Witness statements from anyone who saw the condition at move-out
- A timeline of when you returned keys, when the inspection happened, and when the deduction was first mentioned

## What to Ask For in Writing

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/phone.svg

- An itemized breakdown of the deduction
- Photos of the alleged wall damage and cleaning issues
- The exact reason each amount was withheld
- Copies of any invoices, contractor estimates, or cleaning bills
- A statement showing whether the landlord is claiming actual repair costs or just an estimate
- Confirmation of the remaining deposit balance and when it will be returned
- The legal or contractual basis they rely on for each deduction

## Polite Message to Dispute the Deduction

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/chat-left-text.svg

Subject: Request for itemized explanation of deposit deduction

Dear [Landlord/Agent Name],

Thank you for your message regarding the security deposit after my move-out on 2026-03-15.

I would like to review the deduction in detail. Please send me:
- an itemized breakdown of the amount being withheld,
- photos of the alleged wall damage and cleaning issues,
- copies of any invoices or estimates,
- and the specific basis for each charge.

From my side, I understood the apartment to be returned in a reasonable condition, and I do not agree with the current deduction as stated. Once I have the supporting documents, I can review them and respond.

Please also confirm when the remaining deposit will be returned.

Kind regards,
[Your full name]
[Address / flat number]

## Practical Next Steps

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg

- Send your reply in writing and keep a copy
- Save screenshots and PDFs of everything
- Ask for a deadline to receive the documents
- If the landlord gives only a vague explanation, repeat your request for itemized proof
- Keep your tone calm and factual; avoid admitting liability unless you are sure

## Sources

- Berlin tenant advice overview: https://www.berliner-mieterverein.de/
- German Civil Code, rental deposit rules: https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/
- Berlin consumer/tenant guidance: https://www.verbraucherzentrale-berlin.de/
